title: Not All Change Is Damage: Update-Matched Unlearning for Large Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2610.21230v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Unlearning aims to remove selected knowledge from large language models to mitigate privacy and safety risks while preserving useful capabilities. For models that continue to be fine-tuned after release, this goal is insufficient: they must also resist relearning the deleted knowledge while preserving plasticity, the ability to learn new tasks. Existing defenses train against simulated relearning while trying to preserve useful capabilities, but low relearning alone cannot distinguish selective resistance from a general loss of plasticity. Evaluating preservation after an update requires deciding what the updated model should remain close to. A pre-update reference penalizes useful changes induced by the update simply because they depart from earlier outputs. We therefore formulate the reference-timing hypothesis that, at comparable target suppression, an update-matched reference better preserves plasticity than a pre-update one. To test

translated_title: 并非所有改变都是损害：面向大语言模型的更新匹配遗忘
translated_abstract: 旨在从大语言模型中移除选定知识，以降低隐私和安全风险，同时保留有用的能力。对于发布后仍会持续微调的模型而言，这一目标并不充分：它们还必须在保持可塑性的同时抵抗对已删除知识的重新学习。现有的防御方法通过针对模拟的重新学习进行训练，同时试图保留有用的能力，但仅凭较低的重新学习程度无法区分选择性的抵抗能力与可塑性的整体丧失。要在模型更新后评估保留情况，需要确定更新后的模型应与什么保持接近。若采用更新前的参照，则会仅仅因为更新带来的有益改变偏离了早期输出而对这些改变进行惩罚。因此，我们提出了参照时序假设：在相当的目标抑制水平下，使用更新匹配的参照比使用更新前的参照能更好地保留可塑性。为了测试……（摘要截断）
tldr: 该论文提出“参照时序假设”，证明在大语言模型遗忘任务中，采用更新匹配的参照比更新前的参照能更好地保留模型学习新任务的可塑性，从而有效区分对已删知识的选择性抵抗与整体可塑性丧失。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes the reference-timing hypothesis, showing that an update-matched reference better preserves plasticity than a pre-update one in LLM unlearning, enabling distinction between selective resistance to relearning and a general loss of plasticity.
